The affine theorem uses b at theta*, as specified by referenced J1; other common-anchor diagnostics retain their own declared anchor.

Subtracting the two stationary equations gives Phat d=-Delta g(theta*). Whiten to (I+A)z=-b. Since A is symmetric and ||A||<=epsilon<1, the inverse norm is at most 1/(1-epsilon). For affine qhat the fitted query difference is delta_q(theta*)+Ghat P^-1/2 z. The triangle and operator-norm inequalities give (1), with Lq applied to both the query defect and query derivative for a scaled vector query. No constrained optimum or truth error is covered.

With B=(I+A)^-1, ||B||<=1/(1-eA) and ||B-I||<=eA/(1-eA). Expanding the covariance difference as T(B-I)T^T+TBD^T+DBT^T+DBD^T proves (2) without any commutation assumptions. The covariance formula follows directly from the whitened precision factorization. It is restricted to a common-anchor local GN covariance.

Integrating the exact candidate Hessian over the segment gives Hbar d=-Delta g(theta*) and Hbar>=m P0. Whitening yields the claimed displacement inequality. Integrating the candidate query derivative gives the stated scalar query consequence. Both stationary fits, the segment domain and uniform exact-Hessian lower bound are essential; GN positivity alone is not used.
